                                                                              1                                         NOTICE OF REMOVAL

                                                                              2            In accordance with 28 U.S.C. §§ 1332(d), 1441, and 1446, with full reservation of defenses,

                                                                              3   Defendant Robert Thede (“Thede”) gives notice of the removal of this action originally filed in the

                                                                              4   Superior Court of the State of California, Contra Costa County, to the United States District Court

                                                                              5   for the Northern District of California, Oakland Division. In support of this notice of removal,

                                                                              6   Thede provides the required “short and plain statement of the grounds for removal.” 28 U.S.C. §

                                                                              7   1446(a); see also Dart Cherokee Basin Operating Co. v. Owens, 135 S. Ct. 547, 553 (2014) (“By

                                                                              8   design, § 1446(a) tracks the general pleading requirement stated in Rule 8(a) of the Federal Rules

                                                                              9   of Civil Procedure.”).

                                                                             10   I.       NATURE OF REMOVED ACTION
                        Telephone (213) 205-6520; Facsimile (213) 205-6521
Spertus, Landes & Josephs, LLP




                                                                             11            1.       On September 6, 2024, Plaintiff Lindsey Cannon (“Cannon”) filed a Complaint in
                                  617 West 7th Street, Suite 200
                                     Los Angeles, CA 90017




                                                                             12   the Superior Court of the State of California, Contra Costa County. Plaintiff brings claims under

                                                                             13   California law for alleged violations of California’s Business and Professions Code §§ 17200 and

                                                                             14   17550, and for breach of contract.

                                                                             15            2.       Robert Thede and All Roads Travel LLC are the named Defendants. The

                                                                             16   Complaint also asserts the existence of 10 unnamed “Doe” defendants.

                                                                             17            3.       Cannon is a citizen and resident of California. (Compl. ¶ 4.)

                                                                             18            4.       Thede is a citizen and resident of Nevada. (Compl. ¶ 5.)

                                                                             19            5.       All Roads Travel LLC (“All Roads Travel”) is a limited liability company

                                                                             20   organized under the laws of Delaware. Its members are entities formed under the laws of Nevada

                                                                             21   and California.

                                                                             22            6.       The Complaint seeks $45,000,000 in damages. (Compl. at 14, ¶¶ 5, 6.)

                                                                             23   II.      JURISDICTION

                                                                             24            7.       The Court has jurisdiction under the Class Action Fairness Act.

                                                                             25            8.       Plaintiff brings a class action complaint pursuant to California law, alleging two

                                                                             26   classes—one California class and one nationwide class.

                                                                             27            9.       The putative California class is defined as:

                                                                             28            All individuals, including Plaintiff, who while in California, purchased air or sea

                                                                              2           ownership with JusCollege or otherwise, sold, provided, furnished, contracted for,

                                                                              3           arranged, and/or advertised, but to whom said air or sea transportation or other travel

                                                                              4           services were not actually provided and to whom all moneys paid for such

                                                                              5           unprovided air or sea transportation or other travel services was not returned.

                                                                              6           (Compl. ¶ 15.)

                                                                              7           10.    The putative nationwide class is defined as:

                                                                              8           All individuals, including Plaintiff, who while in the United States, purchased air

                                                                              9           or sea transportation or other travel services that Defendants, due to a unity of

                                                                             10           interest and ownership with JusCollege or otherwise, sold, provided, furnished,

                                  617 West 7th Street, Suite 200

                                                                             12           transportation or other travel services were not actually provided and to whom all

                                                                             13           moneys paid for such unprovided air or sea transportation or other travel services

                                                                             14           was not returned. (Compl. ¶ 20.)

                                                                             15           11.    Plaintiff is a citizen and resident of California. (Compl. ¶ 4.)

                                                                             16           12.    Defendant Thede is a citizen and resident of Nevada. (Compl. ¶ 5.)

                                                                             17           13.    Defendant All Roads Travel is a citizen of California and Nevada. See Johnson v.

                                                                             18   Columbia Props. Anchorage, LP, 437 F.3d 894, 899 (9th Cir. 2006).

                                                                             19           14.    The parties are therefore minimally diverse under 28 U.S.C. § 1332(d)(2)(A) as

                                                                             20   Plaintiff is from a “State different” from Defendant Thede.

                                                                             21           15.    The amount in controversy exceeds the jurisdictional prerequisite of

                                                                             22   $5,000,000.01, 1 because the sum demanded in the Complaint is $45,000,000. (Compl. at 14, ¶¶ 5,

                                                                             23   6.)

                                                                             24           16.    There are more than 100 putative class members. See 28 U.S.C. § 1332(d)(5)(B).

                                                                             25   (Compl. ¶ 21 (alleging that the putative nationwide class contains “at least hundreds of

                                                                             27   not concede liability for the entire amount[.]” Lewis v. Verizon Commc’ns, Inc., 627 F.3d 395, 400
                                                                                  (9th Cir. 2010).

                                                                              2          17.        Because the Complaint alleges a putative nationwide class, Plaintiff will be unable

                                                                              3   to show that “greater than two-thirds of the members of all proposed plaintiff classes in the

                                                                              4   aggregate are citizens of the State in which the action was originally filed.” 28 U.S.C. §

                                                                              5   1332(d)(4).

                                                                              6          18.        Accordingly, the complaint alleges a “class action” with more than 100 members

                                                                              7   under state law; the parties are at least minimally diverse; the amount in controversy exceeds the

                                                                              8   $5,000,000 jurisdictional threshold; and there is no statutory barrier to this Court’s jurisdiction.

                                                                              9   The U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California therefore has removal jurisdiction

                                                                             10   over this matter pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1332(d)(2).

                                                                             11   III.   COMPLIANCE WITH PROCEDURAL REQUIREMENTS
                                  617 West 7th Street, Suite 200
                                     Los Angeles, CA 90017




                                                                             12          15.         Thede has satisfied all the procedural requirements for removal under 28 U.S.C.

                                                                             13   § 1446, and this Court’s Local Rules.

                                                                             14          16.        Thede is filing this Notice of Removal in the United States District Court for the

                                                                             15   Northern District of California because the state court in which the action is pending, the Contra

                                                                             16   Costa Superior Court, is within this federal judicial district. This Notice is signed pursuant to

                                                                             17   Rule 11 of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure.

                                                                             18          17.        Thede was served by waiver and acknowledgement on June 11, 2025. See Exhibit

                                                                             19   A (final page of exhibit). Thede is removing the case within 30 days of that date; therefore, this

                                                                             20   removal is timely under 28 U.S.C. § 1446(b). See Murphy Bros., Inc. v. Michetti Pipe Stringing,

                                                                             21   Inc., 526 U.S. 344, 356 (1999).

                                                                             22          18.        Defendant All Roads Travel’s consent to removal is not required under CAFA,

                                                                             23   Home Depot U. S. A., Inc. v. Jackson, 587 U.S. 435, 445 (2019) (“Section 1453(b) then states that

                                                                             24   [a] class action . . . may be removed by any defendant without the consent of all defendants.”).

                                                                             25          19.        After filing this Notice, in accordance with 28 U.S.C. § 1446(d), Thede will serve

                                                                             26   a copy of this Notice upon the Plaintiff and will file a copy of the Notice with the Clerk of the

                                                                             27   Contra Costa Superior Court.

                                                                             28          20.        Nothing in this Notice of Removal should be interpreted as a waiver or

                                                                              9          22.     Under N.D. Cal. L.R. 3-2(d), this removed matter can be assigned to the Oakland

                                                                             10   Division because it is removed from Contra Costa County. Defendant Thede respectfully
